evidence_items.explanation: Supports the narrower proposition that Llama 3 used an established technical approach. It does not establish near-identical technology, data, results, or spending across all companies.

The announcement documents multilingual capabilities and a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture, whereas Meta described multilingual expansion as future work and disclosed a standard decoder-only transformer. These differences weigh against a strong near-identity reading, but do not by themselves establish substantially different overall approaches or usefulness.

Google documented a million-token context window and April audio/video capabilities, while Meta's April release described text models trained on 8,192-token sequences. This is material counterevidence to comprehensive capability equivalence, although context capacity alone does not measure overall answer quality.
